claim: Entropy H=-sum p log p is the unique uncertainty measure meeting continuity, monotonic growth with equal options, and additivity under splitting a choice; it is the floor on average code length per symbol.
agent_test: Score a probe by expected entropy reduction over a hypothesis list; check on toy tasks that the sum of step gains equals the gain of the whole question plan.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Redundancy of printed English rises as longer context is allowed: about 50% at ~8 letters (1948), about 75% at 100 letters (1951; upper bound 1.3 and lower bound 0.6 bits/letter); a word trigram trained on 583M words gets 1.75 bits/char (cross-entropy upper bound).
agent_test: Not directly testable; context for why more context lowers measured uncertainty (use history in belief updates, S7).

claim: A good predictor is a good compressor: LLM plus arithmetic coding beats gzip/LZMA2 on text (Chinchilla 70B 8.3% vs gzip 32.3% of raw on enwik9) and on images (43.4% vs PNG 58.5%) and audio (16.4% vs FLAC 30.3%).
agent_test: Log-loss of the agent's own model on a held-out task stream as a cheap quality probe.

claim: Compression (bits/char on external text) tracks average benchmark score nearly linearly across LLMs (Pearson -0.93, RMSE 3.1%; single benchmarks -0.88 to -0.95).
agent_test: Check whether per-item answer log-loss predicts item correctness for our agent at equal tokens.

claim: Counting model size matters: bigger models compress big data better but lose on small data once parameter bytes are counted (two-part code); loss fit L=E+A/N^0.34+B/D^0.28 with E=1.69 read as the entropy floor of natural text.
agent_test: None direct; reminder that an entropy floor exists and gains vanish near it.

claim: Token-level entropy confuses wording with meaning; entropy over meaning clusters (semantic entropy, bidirectional entailment) predicts answer correctness better: AUROC 0.77 CoQA and 0.83 TriviaQA (OPT 2.7B-30B) vs 0.66/0.79 for the distinct-answer count.
agent_test: Sample k answers on our tasks, cluster by meaning, compare AUROC of cluster entropy vs majority share vs verbalised confidence at equal tokens. All four lines are one paper (checked against the PDF); Farquhar 2024 is the same group.

claim: Semantic entropy detects confabulation: mean AUROC 0.790 vs naive entropy 0.691, P(True) 0.698, embedding regression 0.687 over 30 task-model combinations, stable 0.78-0.81 for LLaMA 2, Falcon, Mistral 7B-70B.
agent_test: Same as K06 on factual and multi-step tasks; use AURAC (accuracy after refusing top-entropy items) as the metric.

claim: The semantic-entropy result grew from OPT-30B on two datasets (2023) to 30 task-model combinations (2024); gain over naive entropy about 0.10 AUROC. All from one research group, so independence is low.
agent_test: No test; flags low independence.

claim: A linear probe on one generation's hidden state predicts semantic entropy (AUROC 0.7-0.95), removing the 5-10x sampling cost; it beats an accuracy probe in distribution only for some models (+2.8 Mistral-7B, -0.5 Llama-2-7B, long-form -1.9 and -2.0) and generalises better out of distribution.
agent_test: Not applicable to a closed API agent without hidden states; relevant only for an open model.

claim: Entropy signals have limits: a model that is consistently wrong has low semantic entropy (an inference from the definition; Farquhar et al. say it detects only confabulation); sampling temperature trades accuracy against diversity (best AUROC at T=0.5, Kuhn Fig 3b, TriviaQA/OPT-30B); at T=1.5 semantic-equivalence classification accuracy falls to 61% vs over 92% at lower temperatures; tests are mostly factual QA (TriviaQA, CoQA), not multi-step reasoning.
schema_part: G (do not trust low entropy as proof)
agent_test: Run the gate on tasks with systematic errors; measure share of confident-wrong items that pass the gate.
note: Gap search d14: DeepConf reports confident-wrong traces passing the confidence filter (GPT-OSS-120B).
audit_note: Kuhn et al. App. B: 61% (hot, T=1.5) vs over 92% (cooler) is the accuracy of the semantic-equivalence clustering, not the accuracy of sampled answers.
claim_before_audit: Entropy signals have limits: a model that is consistently wrong has low semantic entropy; sampling temperature trades accuracy against diversity (0.5 best in Fig 3b; sample accuracy ~61% hot vs >92% cool); tests are mostly factual QA, not multi-step reasoning.

claim: Self-evaluation P(True)/P(IK) is a weaker baseline: Kadavath 52B models are well calibrated on multiple-choice/true-false in the right format, but Kuhn's 10-shot reimplementation on OPT-30B did worse than semantic entropy; RLHF policies are miscalibrated at T=1.
agent_test: Compare verbalised P(True) vs sample-cluster entropy on our agent.

claim: Choosing each question by expected information gain (EIG) over a filtered hypothesis set roughly doubles 20 Questions success: mean +37.4 points over direct prompting; Animals GPT-4o 45 to 93, GPT-4o-mini 44 to 88, Llama-3.1-8B 8 to 63 (100 targets per cell, se 2-5 points); never decreased. Numbers re-checked against Table 1 of the PDF.
agent_test: Implement hypothesis list + EIG scoring for probe choice, compare to prompt-only probe choice at equal tokens (BED-LLM costs extra LLM calls; paper wall-clock 2h30m vs 3h10m for Entropy on Qwen-72B Animals).

claim: Raw predictive entropy of the answer is weaker than EIG: Animals 88 vs 79 (mini), 93 vs 88 (4o), 63 vs 54 (Llama-8B); Celebrities Qwen-72B 84 vs 59; entropy still beats Split in several cells and gave no gain over Prompt-Only in preference elicitation.
agent_test: A/B: probe score = answer entropy vs EIG over hypotheses; include noisy-answer cases (the ice-cream question has high entropy and EIG 0).

claim: A filtered, coherent hypothesis set is the biggest contributor: removing filtering (ICL Beliefs) drops Animals GPT-4o 93 to 25 and GPT-4o-mini 88 to 18; asking the LLM to pick the most informative question (Implicit Max) reaches 70 on GPT-4o.
agent_test: Ablate hypothesis filtering in the agent's candidate list.
note: Gap search d04: on ARC (GPT-4, n=100) correct hypothesis present in only 49 tasks; 28 of 30 solved tasks had one. Coverage is the bottleneck, supports the claim outside 20 Questions.

claim: Unaided LLM questions have low EIG and ignore the board: Grand 2024 human mean EIG 1.27 (best 3.61, 97% >0; N=40, 605 pairs, 18 boards); GPT-4/CodeLlama at k=1 about 0.65-0.77; sampling k=5 approaches and k=10 exceeds the human mean; k=50 still below the best human.
agent_test: Sample k candidate probes and pick by computed EIG vs one-shot probe, at equal tokens.

claim: Open LLMs improve at 20 Questions by DPO on high- vs low-EIG question pairs: success 56.7% to 68.9%, EIG 0.34 to 0.45; abstract targets stay hard (7.7% to 23.1%). Plain fine-tuning lowered success (46.6%).
agent_test: Training, out of scope for a scaffold-only agent; shows EIG is a valid training signal.

claim: Uncertainty of Thoughts (EIG-scored question trees) raises success 38.1% on average over direct prompting (46.6% Llama3-70B); beats CoT-SC by 33.8, Reflexion 29.9, original ToT 28.3, adapted ToT 12.4; GPT-4 DX 97.0 vs 89.4 (near ceiling); plain CoT hurt on 20Q. Gains largest where the base model is weak and the candidate set is closed.
agent_test: Compare against self-consistency and ToT at matched token count; UoT uses more tokens.

claim: Choosing clarifying questions by EIG over candidate solutions beats reasoning only in question space (20 Questions, code requirements on HumanEval/APPS); the gap shrinks for stronger models and EIG needs more LLM calls.
agent_test: Same design as K11, on code tasks.

claim: In preference elicitation, BOED picks the question and the LM only words it (OPEN) and beats LM-only elicitation; LM-led open questions beat user-written prompts (N=388, GATE).
agent_test: Low priority; metrics differ per study.
audit_note: Li et al. say LM-led elicitation is 'often' more informative than user-written prompts (claim drops 'often'); Handa et al. and Li et al. share several authors (Tamkin, Goodman, Andreas, B. Li), so they are one research group, though the two findings are separate.

claim: ChatGPT is near-optimal at the first half-split on 8 candidates but later questions lose informativeness and it keeps asking after the target is identified (7.24 questions per game); other work agrees LLMs adapt poorly to earlier answers.
agent_test: Add a stop rule: stop probing when posterior entropy over hypotheses is below a threshold; measure wasted probes.
audit_note: Second source (BED-LLM) just cites Bertolazzi et al. and Zhang et al., so 'other work agrees' rests on a citing sentence, not independent evidence.

claim: Information gain per reasoning step (change in log-probability of the correct answer) separates correct from wrong CoT steps in toy arithmetic (0.96, 0.98, 0.06 vs outcome reward model 0.77, 0.98, 0.54).
agent_test: Needs the gold answer, so usable offline for evaluation only.

claim: Policy entropy collapses early in RL for reasoning (over 95% of drop and gain early); fit R = -a exp(H) + b; Clip-Cov/KL-Cov keep entropy and gain 15.0% AIME24 and 14.6% AIME25 on Qwen2.5-32B.
agent_test: Training; scaffold analogue is to keep diverse candidate probes.

claim: Whether humans pick tests by Shannon information gain, probability gain or impact is unsettled: past data could not separate them; optimised experiments favoured probability gain under experience-based learning; a review says optimal experiment design is not yet a good theory of inquiry.
agent_test: Test EIG vs probability gain (expected drop in error) as probe score on our agent; probability gain targets final accuracy directly.

claim: EIG is mutual information (Lindley 1956): expected drop in posterior entropy = I(X;Y); this is the score used by BED-LLM and UoT.
agent_test: Definitional; no test. a27 was not opened by researchers.

claim: Cover and King (1978) gambling estimate of English entropy was about 1.3 bits/letter, in line with Shannon's 1951 upper bound at 100 letters.
agent_test: None; a26 was not opened by researchers (memory only).
note: Gap search d16: could not open Cover-King or Oaksford-Chater text; unverified, no failed-replication data found.

claim: Answer-agreement stop rules cut sampling cost at near-equal accuracy: Early-Stopping SC saves 33.8% (MATH) to 84.2% (Coin Flip) of samples; Adaptive-Consistency saves up to 7.9x; a Beta stability test beats an entropy threshold and a majority-share threshold at equal cost; DeepConf cuts tokens up to 84.7%. No study compares stop rules for EIG-based probe selection.
agent_test: Stop sampling when the Beta-posterior probability that the top answer stays top exceeds a threshold; compare tokens and accuracy with a fixed-N majority vote on BrainTeaser.
audit_note: 'No study compares stop rules for EIG-based probe selection' is an absence claim that opened sources cannot establish.

claim: The share of sampled paths agreeing with the voted answer tracks accuracy on multi-step reasoning (GSM8K), and low-entropy answer sets are mostly correct. But confident-wrong items pass the gate (GPT-OSS-120B overconfidence in DeepConf), so a gate needs an independent check on items it passes.
agent_test: Log top-answer share per ARC/BrainTeaser item; report the accuracy among items with share above 0.8 and list the wrong ones.
audit_note: Early-stopping SC shows lower entropy for correct vs incorrect voted answers (mean difference), so 'mostly correct' is a mild gloss; the closing recommendation is the notes' inference.

claim: Where the hypothesis set must be invented (ARC, GPT-4, n=100), hypothesis generation plus filtering lifts accuracy from 17% direct (23% programs only) to 30%, but a correct hypothesis existed for only 49 tasks, and human-written hypotheses reach 45%. Coverage of the hypothesis list, not the scoring, limits the gain.
agent_test: Measure the share of items whose true rule is in the agent's hypothesis list before any scoring; scoring cannot help below that ceiling.

claim: Conditioning the answer-likelihood prompt on the whole dialogue history lowered 20 Questions success in 13 of 15 model-dataset cells versus a static likelihood (e.g. Animals GPT-4o 93 vs 86), attributed to context-induced calibration shifts.
agent_test: A/B: probe-scoring prompt with and without S-state history; keep history in the belief set only.

claim: For RLHF chat models, verbalised probabilities (especially over several guesses) are better calibrated than token probabilities or sampled label agreement on factual QA, with expected calibration error cut by a relative 50% (Tian 2023). Not tested on multi-step reasoning items.
agent_test: Ask for top-3 guesses with probabilities per item; compute ECE on a held-out ARC/BrainTeaser slice.

claim: Models are weak at choosing the clarifying question when the task is logic or planning: best models score 40-50% on QuestBench Logic-Q and Planning-Q while near ceiling on arithmetic; accuracy falls with search depth; solving the full problem does not imply asking the right question.
agent_test: Compare unaided probe choice with explicit hypothesis-tree probe choice on logic-style items.

claim: Chinchilla irreducible loss E = 1.69 is most likely nats per token (about 2.44 bits per token; a 70B/1.4T prediction of 1.94 nats is about 0.70 bits per byte, near the reported 0.667 on The Pile). Unit is inferred, not stated, and the floor applies to web text, not to puzzle answers.
agent_test: None; context only. Do not compare E to Shannon bits per letter.
